_provenance.note: Kentucky citation authorities. Kentucky's operative SNAP policy lives in the Division of Family Support Operation Manual, Volume 2 (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) and its companion Volume IIA (SNAP Work Requirements), both cited by 'MS' (Material Section) number — e.g. 'MS 5000' (Resource Maximums), 'MS 3160' (Categorical Eligibility), 'MS 5490' (Standard Utility Allowance). Kentucky's own manual does not append a program suffix to its MS numbers the way Louisiana's 'B-1040-SNAP' does, so this pack writes 'KY MS' before a citation in running prose purely for cross-state disambiguation (matching this roster's general convention), while the regex below matches the bare 'MS ####' form Kentucky's own manual uses natively. This pack ALSO cites a real, separate Kentucky Revised Statute (KRS 205.2005) for the drug-felony opt-out finding, so this pack defines a SECOND citation family, 'KRS 205.', matching this roster's Alabama and Louisiana packs' two-family pattern.

patterns.note: Kentucky Division of Family Support Operation Manual, Volume 2 (SNAP) or Volume IIA (SNAP Work Requirements), Material Section number, e.g. MS 5000 (Resource Maximums), MS 3160 (Categorical Eligibility), MS 5200 (Income Eligibility Scale), MS 2100 (ABAWD Work Requirements).
Kentucky Revised Statutes, Chapter 205 (Public Assistance and Medical Assistance), cited by section number. This pack cites exactly one: KRS 205.2005, the drug-felony SNAP/TANF opt-out statute.

kyms.note: ABAWD Overview — 18-64 age range, under-14 caregiver exemption, 3 countable months in a 36-month period absent compliance
ABAWD Work Requirements — 80 hours/month (paid, self-employed, in-kind, or volunteer work), 20 hours/week WIOA/TAA participation, or E&T program participation; waived-county exemption
ABAWD Exemptions — 17-and-under/65-and-older, medically unfit, household member under 14, pregnant, living in a waived county
Criminals — fleeing felons and probation/parole violators; disqualification lasts until the condition stops
Child Support Disqualification Overview — $500+ in child support arrearages disqualifies the obligated individual until compliant, identified via automated KASES matching
Child Support Disqualification Exemptions — specific criteria verified by Family Support or DCSS staff

Categorical Eligibility — CE (KTAP/Kinship/WIN/FAST/SSI recipients, no income or resource test) and ECE (TANF-info-sheet recipients; 130% FPL for non-elderly/disabled, 200% FPL for all-elderly/disabled, resource test waived for both tracks)

Verification at Application — CE households have resources, SSN, residency, and sponsored-alien status treated as met; ECE households meet all factors except SSN and remain subject to the 200% FPL/net income standards
Simplified Assistance for the Elderly (SAFE) Overview — SSI-recipient one/two-person households age 60+, 36-month certification, no interview
SAFE Eligibility criteria
SAFE Allotments — flat amount based on shelter cost and household size only
Elderly Simplified Application Project (ESAP) Overview — broader elderly/disabled no-earned-income households, 36-month certification, no interview, periodic reporting waived
Transitional SNAP (TSNAP) — Ineligible Households, current disqualification-category list (no drug-felony category present)
Resource Maximums — $3,000 standard / $4,500 households with a disabled member or a member 60+, applicable only to non-CE/non-ECE households
Resources - Excluded — dated 2010, retains a stale 'drug-related felony disqualification' reference not scrubbed after KRS 205.2005's 2021 opt-out

Countable Resources for non-CE/non-ECE households — cash, checking/savings, CDs, stocks, bonds, cryptocurrency, crowdfunding balances, lump-sum lottery/gambling winnings; vehicles absent from the list entirely
Resources Which May or May Not Be Counted — jointly held accounts, battered-individual-shelter resources, etc.
Income Eligibility Scale — current FFY2026 figures effective October 1, 2025 (130%/165%/200% FPL gross columns, net income column by household size)

Deductions - General — Standard Deduction ($209/$223/$261/$299), Standard Medical Deduction ($137), capped excess shelter deduction ($744), Homeless Shelter Deduction ($199 in lieu of ordinary shelter deduction)
Members Eligible for Medical Deduction — elderly (60+) or disabled member; special presumptive/emergency SSI payment provisions
Standard Utility Allowance (SUA) — $388/month flat for all household sizes, for households with heating/cooling costs
Basic Utility Allowance (BUA) — $331/month; standalone Telephone Standard $64/month
Treatment of Utility Expenses — SUA/BUA-eligible households must use the standard, not actual expenses
Child Support Deduction — ordinary deduction (7 CFR 273.9(d)(5)) for legally obligated child support paid to a non-household member, capped at the legally obligated amount
Special Considerations for Specific Households — current disqualified-member deduction handling (IPV, fleeing felons, work-requirement noncompliance); no drug-felony category present
Overview of Application Time Standards — 30 calendar days ordinary processing; 5-calendar-day expedited-service ceiling (faster than the federal 7-day floor)
Expedited Services Criteria — plain federal gates: gross income under $150 and liquid resources $100 or less; combined income/resources less than shelter costs; destitute migrant/seasonal farmworker
Special Issuance Timeframes for Expedited Services — 5-calendar-day standard, including DAA-treatment-center and battered-persons-shelter residents
Assigning Certification Periods — three-tier structure: 4 months (non-exempt ABAWD households), 12 months (default), 36 months (all-60+-RSDI/SSI-no-earned-income households)

Simplified Reporting Households — all Kentucky SNAP households are Simplified Reporting by default; mid-period reporting triggers at the household's own FPL ceiling (130% or 200%), ABAWD hours drop, or substantial lottery/gambling winnings
Household Failure to Cooperate — dated 2021, retains a 'Drug felons' category label among household members who must cooperate; not itself an active eligibility disqualification

kykrs.note: Opt-out of 21 U.S.C. sec. 862a(a) — effective June 29, 2021 (2021 Ky. Acts ch. 182, sec. 4) — exempts ALL individuals residing in Kentucky from the federal drug-felony SNAP/TANF disqualification. A FULL opt-out, confirmed by direct primary-source read (no access barrier) and independently by omission in KY's own current disqualification lists
